column1: # Every statement the site makes about U-Board, its status, and where this repository backs it.
# Not published: it sits outside public/ and the build never reads it. test/claims.test.ts matches its ids against
# the data-claim ids in src/ (both ways) and checks that every ref exists. Change a sentence, change its row in the same commit.
# status: works = works today · design = how it is built (a principle or a boundary) · vision = a goal, not built yet · promise = an operating commitment
# ref: one or more repository paths, joined with " · ".

column4: People write a board in the editor and AI through the MCP server, the same JSON document; the same viewer draws it; the document places its parts over a drawing or on a grid; values are read from the owning system while the view is open (an open board re-reads every 30 s)

The board at the top of the home page is one board of the gallery (the same pack, the same library viewer, drawn when the page runs script; its thumbnail otherwise), and a line under it says whether its values are a source's recorded answers or example data

The small drawing in the states section is drawn by the library viewer from a sample adapter kept in the page, on purpose, to show the three states at once: live unframed, stale dashed amber, disconnected dotted grey; reason and age in the text. Its caption says so. The static drawing is what a browser without script shows

A board is one JSON document (data, parts, layout) in one language, placed over a drawing (canvas) or on a grid; every gallery board is checked against it; the check names a mistake by its JSON path; any gallery board's document can be edited in the playground
Per-value quality, the four reasons, the age of a stale value, no whole-view error
Generic HTTP connector: static token/header or OAuth 2.0 client credentials, JSON Pointer, credentials server-side and sealed at rest
Share link: read-only without sign-in, iframe embedding, optional expiry, revocation

The board at the top is a gallery board drawn by the library viewer from the example answers of its pack, and building a board can be tried on the playground page (both backed by the site code); the demo instance iyulab operates for invited accounts is an operating commitment, not something the code proves
One image with server, console and share viewer; runs without internet access (no outside calls but those configured); PostgreSQL or the embedded database
The npm packages @iyulab/u-board (the board language and the viewer, MIT, repository iyulab/U-Board) and @iyulab/u-board-designer (the authoring view, AGPL-3.0-or-later)
No symbol library, alarm handling or control output; a board's action toward another board only asks the host to go there
Boards store binding references, not values
No warehouse charts or pivot tables

Two licenses: the library @iyulab/u-board (board language and viewer) is MIT, in its own repository iyulab/U-Board; the product in this repository (authoring view, server, console, MCP server) is AGPL-3.0-or-later with a commercial license available

Sample boards (packages/samples), drawn by the library viewer from recorded answers (SnapshotAdapter); on public open data the same document binds the live source through the HTTP connector (path key, list items by field), and an open share link re-reads every 30 s; fields with no public source are drawn on example data, labelled as such and never offered to an installation (isInstallable)
The authoring view the library ships, in the page, on the sample board and source; saving keeps the board in the browser (localStorage)

The chat panel beside the board editor draws the open board with the MCP server's tools, checks it with look drawn in the page, and calls the model the person sets from the browser (key kept there); the film is a recording of it with qwen3.8-27b, sped up ten times, on example values

A gallery board's published definition and data, edited as text and drawn by the library viewer as typed; problems named by JSON path (checkBoard for the definition, the data's shape checked); nothing leaves the page
